33 one third of the Virtual Training Sessions took place on identified topics to fill knowledge and skill gaps of BIsThe BIC Africa Virtual Training Centre was launched in November 2023. The 2023 annual online training course was comprised of 4 training sessions of 4 hours each and took the business incubator managers of the Country Projects but also beyond as the training was open for registration to BIs from SubSaharan African countries through an Introduction to Incubation and Ecosystems to Business Model Canvas in the first two sessions. Sessions three and four were then dedicated to Engaging with Investors. These topics were identified following consultation with the implementing partners of the country projects and based on BIC Africa teams experience regarding BIs knowledge and skill gaps in the 5 target countries specifically. There were 67 participants in the session that took place on the 29th of November 2023 and 190 participants in total for the three sessions that took place in December 2023. The topics of the 2024 and 2025 editions will be finetuned based on the feedback received from the questionnaire that was sent at the end of the 2023 edition regarding the needs of the participants and request for future subjects to tackle as well as the feedback of participants of the BIC Africa Boot Camps that took place in 2023. As such it will be ensured that the sessions will fit the knowledge and skill gaps of the participants.In addition prior to the launch of the Virtual Training Centre 1 online training took place between the 22nd and the 24th of June 2021.

description.narrative: Increase in the number of small businesses

comment.narrative: 388 value based on the companies assisted through the BIs in the scope of the 5 Country Projects programmes.Regarding this indicator data is retrieved through the implementing partners of the Country Projects as they are directly monitoring the BIs involved in their respective programmes and is currently only partially available as the Country Projects started with delay and thus some of the selected incubators are at an early phase of working with companies under the Programmes. A breakdown per Country Project is provided below.BIC Ethiopia Country Projecto324 entrepreneurs from 157 startups benefited from new business support services specifically the starter programme of BIC Ethiopia which incorporates the aspect of support with setting up a legal entity.o102 MSMEs benefited from new business support services specifically the catalyser incubation programme of BIC Ethiopia.Note The number of all training participants equals to 803 164 Training of Trainers 558 startercatalyser 28 finance Training of Trainers 53 basic financial literacy.BIC Somali Country Project 61 companies have been supported so far by the three business incubators involved in the project and completed the incubation programme. Out of the 61 42 Businesses are Startups with six months to 1 year old while 19 of them are business ideas and as such were supported with establishing a legal entity.Note the data on whether they are registered or not is not available. The concept of registration in Somalia has complexities. Some units register with Ministry of Industry some with Chamber of Commerce and some with the local municipality.Angola Country Project 30 companies have been supported in total so far out of which 20 were actively supported through the two business incubators involved in the project. Out of these 2 were not registered yet and as such were supported with establishing a legal entity. The project is also supporting two other startups in getting the required license for their business operations.Madagascar Incuboost Country Project Data is not yet available as the project started in May 2023 and is in early phases.Comoros APILE Country Project 38 SMEs have been directly supported by the APILE project.Note Based on additional enquiry undertaken by the APILE project and the answers of 6 out of 16 Incubators that the project supports in 2022 the number of entrepreneurs and startups supported was 240 and in 2023 this number grew to 450. Nevertheless this data considers SMEs that are supported by the Comorian incubators beyond the scope of the APILE programme and as such is not taken directly into consideration for the logframe value.Further details can be found in the Annual Narrative report for 2023.
